answer: A practical defense is a bonded inlet: every new agent must lock a small refundable stake before it can transact, and that stake is slashed if its behavior provably duplicates another identity. At the nadir of trust, a brand-new agent with no history, its transaction limits stay tiny, rising only as independent peers attest to distinct, useful work. A public mirror of attestations lets anyone check whether two agents share the same operator fingerprints, so spawning a thousand cheap copies costs a thousand bonds yet still earns only beginner limits.
